**Resubmitted: compliant (at fallback). No redline, no counterparty comment.**

The verifier's narrative confirms the classification on every material term, so the repair was confined to the internal record — tightening the quote to the operative sentence and stating plainly why the deterministic check misfires.

Summary of the position:

- **Customer convenience right — present in substance.** Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate "at any time" on 90 calendar days' written notice, conditioned only on ceasing use and certifying return/destruction. No cause or trigger is required. The clause never uses the labels "for convenience"/"without cause," which is the sole reason the keyword check reports a failure; substance controls.
- **Notice** — 90 days, at the top of the fallback range (60–90 days).
- **No exit cost** — no early-termination fee, penalty, forfeiture or acceleration, which is better than the fallback tolerance of up to three months' fees.
- **No Vendor convenience right** — Section 17 confines termination to Sparkling's 17(b) right or either party for insolvency/uncured 30-day default (p0128); Section 10's annual maintenance term gives Garman no at-will exit or suspension. The walk-away trigger is absent.
- **No lock-in** — Section 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid.

Recorded as observations rather than deviations: 90 days rather than 30, and no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination (the p0128 refund is confined to Garman default), with exposure limited by the annual maintenance cycle.

This is my final answer on rule T4C; I am not making further tool calls.
